Then I round it out with Real Estate and Healthcare as a satalite (LAND/VICI/O & IHI) I'm nervous, but since I own so many bonds, Tbill ladders, and my property in my larger retirement fund and taxable whatever happens is what it is. @goldmanstarch When I see comments like this one from @shabpnd481 pointing towards fundamentals; it becomes clear how the street gets retail to bag hold through this bubble. Retail sees the earnings, the "growth," and says "but Dell is only at 18x earnings,,," They don't comprehend that those earnings multiples are based on cheap credit never drying up; those credit lines themselves often based on a company's stock valuations, GPU collateralized loans, or infinite series pyramid schemes designed to get to IPO and dump on the open market (as Uber and Lyft venture capitol did.) As soon as a slight macroeconomic shock (hormuz....) hit the house of cards, the whole thing begins crashing like the titanic.... slow motion unwind style... and even as water comes flooding in; they keep saying "but its the Titanic, its unsinkable!" Ill take your spot on the life raft.

The 60/40 myth is what commercial banks convinced retail is a good idea because it generates backstopping for their own leveraging which are often backed by bond collateral.
